title: Reconstruct Itinerary
pattern: Eulerian path (Hierholzer): add an airport when it is a dead end
statement: You are given airline `tickets` as pairs `[from, to]`. Build the itinerary that starts at `"JFK"` and uses **every ticket exactly once**. If several itineraries are possible, return the one that is smallest in alphabetical order.

example.why: Flying to KUL first would be alphabetically smaller, but KUL is a dead end: the other two tickets could never be used.

idea: Always taking the alphabetically smallest ticket can run into a **dead end** while tickets are still unused (here: JFK → KUL).

Key insight: an airport where we get **stuck** (no unused ticket left) must be the **last** stop of whatever is still unplaced. So record airports at the moment we get stuck, and the route is built **from the end backwards**.
That is a DFS that appends an airport *after* all its tickets are used (post-order). Reversing the list at the end gives the itinerary.

complexity.timeWhy: Sorting the E tickets dominates; the DFS itself uses every ticket exactly once.
complexity.spaceWhy: The adjacency lists, the route and the recursion stack.

steps.text: Our example: **`tickets = [["JFK","KUL"],["JFK","NRT"],["NRT","JFK"]]`**. Each step runs one highlighted line of the code.
